info.title: OpenVibe.Codes API
info.description: Routes of OpenVibe.Codes as the OpenVibe contracts describe them (openvibe-contracts 0.51.0): each operation lists the capabilities it performs; a token for the service's audience must carry one of them unless the route is open. Generated by openvibe-contracts lib/openapi.js; do not edit.

codes.app-manifest.v1.title: AppManifest
codes.app-manifest.v1.description: PROPOSAL (OpenVibe.Codes, roadmap Wave 20): an app release as the platform knows it. The app is a Network developer app (ADR-014): its id is the Network app id, its capabilities are only a request (the grants in Network are the authority), and trust tiers are metadata that never change a grant check. OpenVibe.Codes validates with this schema, loaded into openvibe-contracts' validator, until Contracts publishes it as codes.app-manifest@1.

id.description: The Network app id (its client_id). Its principal subject is app:<id>.

publisher.description: Who publishes the release: the app itself or a member of its project.

project_id.description: The Network project that owns the app. Tenancy in other services is keyed by it (ADR-014).

environment.description: The app's environment. Apps never change environment.

capabilities.description: Capability ids the app asks for (3+ segments). Only active public (or partner, by staff allowance) capabilities can ever be granted to apps.

consumes.description: Event types (or a trailing .* family) the app subscribes to.

redirect_uris.description: Informational copy of the redirect URIs registered in Network (Network's list is the authority).

contracts.description: Semver range of openvibe-contracts releases it was built against.

sdk.description: Semver range of openvibe-sdk releases it uses.

codes.release-manage-request.v1.title: CodesReleaseManageRequest
codes.release-manage-request.v1.description: codes.release-manage-request@1: bodies of codes.release.manage on OpenVibe.Codes (an app token managing its own releases). POST /api/v1/apps/:app/releases: { kind?, manifest, notes?, publish? } — kind mod or app (anything else is app); manifest must validate as codes.app-manifest@1 for an app or mods.mod-manifest@1 for a mod (422 manifest.invalid with the validation otherwise; a version that already has a release is 409); notes are cut to 2000 characters; publish true publishes the draft at once. POST /api/v1/releases/:id/deprecate: { reason, replacement? } (a reason is required, cut to 500 characters; replacement must be a published release of the same app). POST /api/v1/releases/:id/revoke: { reason } (required). POST /api/v1/releases/:id/publish takes no body. Unknown fields are ignored.

codes.release-manage-result.v1.title: CodesReleaseManageResult
codes.release-manage-result.v1.description: codes.release-manage-result@1: answers of codes.release.manage on OpenVibe.Codes (an app token managing its own releases). POST /api/v1/apps/:app/releases → 201 { release, warnings } (a draft, or published at once with publish: true; manifest validation warnings); POST /api/v1/releases/:id/publish | deprecate | revoke → { release, event_id } (the codes.release.* event announcing it; null when a revoke announced nothing). Refusals are problem+json: 401 auth.required, 403 release.forbidden (another app's release), 409 release.not_draft, 422 with validation errors.

codes.release-read-result.v1.title: CodesReleaseReadResult
codes.release-read-result.v1.description: codes.release-read-result@1: answers of codes.release.read on OpenVibe.Codes (public; no token needed, but a token that is presented must hold the capability; never drafts). GET /api/v1/apps/:app/releases → { app_id, trust, releases } (published, deprecated and revoked releases, newest first); GET /api/v1/apps/:app/trust → { app_id, tier, note, set_by, set_at, note_on_authority } (metadata only: grants in OpenVibe.Network are the authority); GET /api/v1/releases/:id → { release, manifest } (the manifest as published: codes.app-manifest@1 for an app, mods.mod-manifest@1 for a mod). An id that is not an app or a release is 404.

codes.release.v1.title: CodesRelease
codes.release.v1.description: codes.release@1: one release of an app or mod as OpenVibe.Codes presents it (server/domain/releases.js view): its lifecycle (draft → published → deprecated or revoked), compatibility ranges and the app's trust tier (metadata only; grants in OpenVibe.Network are the authority). The manifest itself is served separately (codes.app-manifest@1).

common.no-body.v1.title: NoBody
common.no-body.v1.description: common.no-body@1: the capability's request carries no body; its parameters are the path and query of the routes in implementedBy (an id, a page cursor). An input schema that says so explicitly, so every active capability names one (roadmap WS-C task 4).

errors.problem.v1.title: Problem
errors.problem.v1.description: RFC 9457 problem details (application/problem+json) with a stable OpenVibe error code and trace identifiers. The legacy 'error' string is allowed during migration so existing clients keep working.

error.description: Deprecated compatibility field: same text as title/detail for clients that read {error}.

identity.subject-ref.v1.title: SubjectRef
identity.subject-ref.v1.description: The one cross-platform reference to an actor. Issued by OpenVibe.Network. Never a service-local integer id.

media.media-ref.v1.title: MediaRef
media.media-ref.v1.description: Reference to a Media object. Canonical ids (med_<ULID>) arrive with the Wave 4 object model; until then legacy:<app>:<kind>:<id> addresses today's VOD/clip/file/paste/thumbnail rows.

mods.mod-manifest.v1.title: ModManifest
mods.mod-manifest.v1.description: A mod as the platform knows it (ADR-013): who publishes it, which runtime runs it, which capabilities it asks for and the resources it may use. Requested capabilities are only a request: the install's approved subset is the grant, and trust tiers are install metadata that never change a grant check. The runtime-specific payload (a data pack, a script bundle) is not part of the manifest. 1.1.0 (openvibe-contracts v0.34.0) adds the optional permissions.readGrants and writeGrants, billingHooks and dependencies (ADR-013 amendment of 2026-09-24); every 1.0.0 manifest stays valid.

id.description: Stable mod id; its principal subject is mod:<id>.

publisher.description: Who publishes the mod (a user or an app subject).

target.description: Where the mod runs: <service>.<surface>, e.g. games.browser, games.source, live.overlay.

runtime.description: Runtime adapter and its major version, e.g. games-content@1 (declarative data pack) or source-quickjs@1.

capabilities.description: Capability ids the mod asks for (3+ segments). The target runtime binds only those it implements, and only once granted.

events.description: Event types the mod wants delivered to it.

modules.description: User-module namespaces the mod wants to read or write (a trailing .* names a family). A namespace listed here may be read and written; readGrants and writeGrants (1.1.0) say which.

mediaNamespaces.description: Media namespaces the mod wants to read or write. A namespace listed here may be read and written; readGrants and writeGrants (1.1.0) say which.

readGrants.description: 1.1.0: namespaces the mod may only read. A namespace that is only here is read-only. The install's approved subset is still the grant.

modules.description: User-module namespaces (a trailing .* names a family).

writeGrants.description: 1.1.0: namespaces the mod may read and write. A write needs the namespace here, or in the older modules and mediaNamespaces lists, which mean read and write.

modules.description: User-module namespaces (a trailing .* names a family).

resources.description: The budget the mod asks for. Runtimes meter it; the sandbox that enforces it lives in OpenVibe.Host (Stage C).

cpuMs.description: CPU milliseconds per tick (game runtimes) or per request.

outboundHosts.description: Hosts the mod may reach over the network. Empty or absent = none.

assets.description: Assets the mod ships, as Media object references.

runtime.description: Semver range of the runtime this release works with, e.g. ">=1.0.0 <2.0.0".

contracts.description: Semver range of openvibe-contracts releases it was built against.

billingHooks.description: 1.1.0: how the mod takes part in money, only through Billing and VIP primitives (ADR-013 amendment, ADR-012). entitlement: the mod checks that the person holds this entitlement (billing.entitlement.check or vip.entitlement.check, granted like any other capability). checkout: the mod sends the person to the platform's own checkout for this plan (vip.membership.checkout or a Billing intent). A mod never takes payment, sees payment details or holds a balance. Prices live in Billing and VIP, never in the manifest.

key.description: The entitlement or plan key as Billing and VIP name it, e.g. vip.plan:pln_01jab… (lowercase, the form search.index-document@1 acl.entitlements uses).

description.description: What it unlocks or sells, shown at install.

dependencies.description: 1.1.0: other mods this release needs. A runtime refuses to enable the mod while a required dependency is not installed, not enabled or outside its range. An optional one is used only when present.

version.description: Semver range of the dependency's releases this release works with, e.g. ">=1.2.0 <2.0.0".

openvibeToken.description: An OpenVibe Network token for this service: a person's token, an app token (client credentials, audience of the service) or a first-party service token. Its `cap` claim must include the capability the operation names.
